MetaCONCUR 0.0.0.1
  • Reference

    Procedure for Estimating Score Statistic and Covariance Matrix Components

    CONCUR_worker.Rd

    Estimate the summary statistic and variance components for each chromosome.

    CONCUR_worker(
  cnvData,
  phenoData,
  cutoff.dup,
  cutoff.del,
  formula,
  covData,
  phenoType = c("bin", "cont"),
  chr = "all",
  use.big.memory = FALSE,
  save_dir = NULL
)

    Arguments

    cnvData

    A data.frame object. The CNV event data.

    phenoData

    A data.frame object. The phenotype data.

    cutoff.dup

    A numeric scalar. The cutoff at which TYPE values are deemed to be duplicates.

    cutoff.del

    A numeric scalar. The cutoff at which TYPE values are deemed to be deletions

    formula

    A formula object. The model. Must be of the form LHS ~ RHS.

    covData

    A data.frame object. The covariates. Must include column ID.

    phenoType

    A character object. Must be one of "bin" or "cont" indicating that that phenotype of interest is binary or continuous, respectively.

    chr

    A character of integer object. If character, must be "all" indicating all chromosomes present in cnvData. If integer, one or more chromosomes present in cnvData. The score statistic and variance components will be returned only for those chromosomes specified here.

    use.big.memory

    A logical. If TRUE, large matrix objects are handled as file-backed matrices. Using the feature significantly impacts computation speed and should be used only when matrices are too large to store in RAM.

    save_dir

    A directory path where summary statistics will be saved. If use.big.memory equal to TRUE, must provide a relative path, the folder will be created inside the current working directory (getwd()). For example, "study1" will create ~/study1 directory.

    Value

    A list object. Each element is itself a list corresponding to one or more chromosomes specified in chr and contains:

    grid

    A vector of the grid boundaries.

    SSA

    The score statistic for group A.

    SSB

    The score statistic for group B.

    HAHA

    An 2L x 2L matrix.

    HAHB

    An 2L x 2L matrix.

    HBHB

    An 2L x 2L matrix.

    HAX

    An 2L x p matrix of H_A x.

    HBX

    An 2L x p matrix of H_B x.

    Examples

    # Load example data
data(cnvData)
data(phenoData)
data(covData)
# Run on example data, first 100 individuals
s1_cnv <- cnvData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", cnvData$ID)) >= 1 &
                   as.numeric(sub("P", "", cnvData$ID)) <= 100, ]
s1_pheno <- phenoData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", phenoData$ID)) >= 1 &
                       as.numeric(sub("P", "", phenoData$ID)) <= 100, ]
s1_cov <- covData[as.numeric(sub("P", "", covData$ID)) >= 1 &
                   as.numeric(sub("P", "", covData$ID)) <= 100, ]
cutoff.dup <- 2.3
cutoff.del <- 1.7
formula_bin <- PHEB ~ SEX
s1_SS <- CONCUR_worker(
  cnvData = s1_cnv,
  phenoData = s1_pheno,
  cutoff.dup = cutoff.dup,
  cutoff.del = cutoff.del,
  formula = formula_bin,
  covData = s1_cov,
  phenoType = "bin",
  chr = 1,
  use.big.memory = FALSE,
  save_dir = NULL
)
#> No save_dir provided, summary statistics not saved for chr1
# Output is a list of summary statistics
names(s1_SS)
#> [1] "chr1"
names(s1_SS$chr1)
#> [1] "grid" "SSA"  "SSB"  "HAHA" "HAHB" "HBHB" "HAX"  "HBX"
